About this plan

High-Protein Pepperoni Mac Meal Prep Week — boxed mac and cheese, made to work harder with three simple swaps. Monday: cook a double batch of Annie's Super Mac shells, whisk the cheese packets into whole milk, fold in the shells, then chop and fold in turkey pepperoni. Portion into full and smaller servings across the week — same creamy pepperoni mac for everyone, no separate kid meal and no butter. Wednesday reheats the reserved portions with a splash of milk. Friday steak-and-fries. Full serving: about 370 cal / 25g protein; child portions sized to appetite and intentionally not published. This week runs a DOUBLE batch — the grocery quantities below are already doubled — so the batch covers every night through Saturday.

Pepperoni Mac Batch Cook20 min · 2 adult + 2 kid plates

High-Protein Pepperoni Mac Meal Prep

20 min — this week is a double batch (the grocery amounts below are already doubled). Cook and drain the shells from all the boxes per the package. Whisk every cheese packet into whole milk (1 cup per 3 boxes) until smooth — no butter. Fold the shells into the sauce, then chop the turkey pepperoni and fold it through evenly. Portion into full servings for the adults and smaller servings sized to the kids' appetites. Each 3-box batch is two family dinners for 2A+2K, so the double batch = four dinners: half feeds tonight + Tuesday, half holds for Wednesday + Thursday. Refrigerate the portions in airtight containers.

KID

Steak Night20 min · 4 servings

Steak & Fries with Chimichurri

20 min — Checkers/Rally's frozen fries in the air fryer first (12-15 min), bavette steak seared 2-3 min per side in a hot stainless pan while fries finish, pork breakfast patties cooked in the same pan during the 5-min steak rest. No-judge chimichurri = Spiceology Chimichurri Blend + olive oil + red wine vinegar + chili flakes (mix, sit 5 min). Adults get sliced bavette + fries + chimichurri; kids get cut-up pork patties + fries + raw carrots. ~45g protein / 620 cal per adult. Cross-link to No-Judge Chimichurri cookbook entry.

ADULT

Sliced bavette + Checkers fries + spoonful of chimichurri over the steak

KID

Cut-up pork breakfast patties + fries + raw carrots (no sauce)

Weeknight Picanha with Chimichurri & Frozen Greens

Approximately 480 cal / 40g protein per adult plate. 2 adult plates + 2 deconstructed kid plates. Adults get 6 oz salt-seared picanha, one label serving of Whole Foods Market European Greens with basil-and-garlic sauce, and one label serving of prepared chimichurri spooned over the steak. Kids get two Amylu chicken breakfast patties, half a serving of the same greens, and a toasted slider bun served separately so they can assemble a sandwich or eat the components independently. Two skillets, one cook, done in 25 minutes. Creator pull temp is 135°F for medium; USDA-recommended pull is 145°F + 3 min rest — both preserved on the page. Costco Fotis Fine Foods Chimichurri is the shortcut; the No-Judge Chimichurri cookbook entry is the homemade alternative.

Chili Mac and Cheese

~380 cal / 39g protein per adult container. 8 meal-prep containers: 4 adult (2 oz dry Carbe Diem elbows + 1 full chili serving + one-quarter of the adult sauce build) + 4 kid (1.5 oz dry Barilla regular elbows + half a chili serving + one-quarter of the kid sauce build). Blended cottage-cheese sauce (cottage cheese + Fairlife + nutritional yeast + cheddar powder) split 2:1 into adult and kid pots. Velveeta melts in per pot (2 oz adult / 1 oz kid). Reserved Hot Dog Chili Base folds in (4 full servings adult pot / 2 full-serving equivalents split across 4 kid containers = half chili serving per kid). Bone broth loosens to creamy. Kid macros intentionally not published — cottage cheese fat percentage was not label-verified. Reheats to 165°F all week with a small splash of milk or bone broth if the sauce tightens.

15-Minute Chicken Tikka Masala Split Plate

540 cal / 50g protein per adult plate, 405 cal / 38g protein per kid plate. Serves 2 adults + 2 kids from one 36 oz twin-pack. Warm the sealed Sukhi's Costco tikka masala pouches in hot water 5-7 min while the rumali rotis thaw. Empty into a saucepan, cover, heat 5 min stirring once until steaming. REMOVE 3 SERVINGS (1.5 per kid) BEFORE adding chili — this is the split point. Stir 1 tsp Kashmiri chili into the remaining 4 adult servings and heat briefly to bloom. Adults get 2 servings + 2 rotis plated together. Kids get 1.5 servings + 1.5 rotis, chicken/gravy/rotis in separate compartments for self-dipping. Same tikka, same rotis, split at the pot — this is not scratch-made curry; it's a realistic busy-parent dinner strategy. HALAL claim requires verifying the specific Sukhi's package before publishing — ships pork-free only by default.

Viral Tomato Feta Chicken Pasta, Split Plate Style

The lockdown-era viral tomato-feta pasta adapted into a split-plate meal prep. One casserole roasts 600 g cherry and pear tomatoes with two 8 oz blocks of feta and Mediterranean seasoning at 400°F for 45 min. Air-fry 2 lb chicken thighs in parallel for 20 min. Mash the baked feta and tomatoes into a creamy sauce with visible tomato pieces, chop the chicken, and split 2:1 — ~2/3 of the sauce and chicken to a low-carb penne pot for the adults (2 oz dry per adult container), ~1/3 to a regular penne pot for the smaller portions (1.5 oz dry per container). Pack 6 adult containers plus 6 smaller containers = 3 family dinners for 2 adults + 2 kids. Adult macro headline is ~450 cal / 37g protein; smaller-portion macros intentionally not published — the creator serves 1/2 unit per kid and adjusts to appetite. Refrigerate up to 5 days.

Viral Dumpling Lasagna, Proteinized

A leaner, higher-protein take on @april_eatz's viral dumpling lasagna (discovered via @smallersam). 51 wonton wrappers layered 15 / 9 / 12 / 15 with a 50/50 mix of 93/7 lean ground chicken and 95/5 lean ground pork, soy sauce, rice vinegar, umami seasoning, ginger-garlic paste, and scallions. Bake covered at 400 F for 30 min after pouring 1 cup chicken broth over the top. Rest 5-10 min, cut into 6 servings, drizzle soy and finish with scallions. Household batch: 2 adults + 2 kids for 2 dinners; kids get half servings adjusted for appetite in Tushar's build (kid macros intentionally not published). French Dip Polenta Dunkers

Episode 3 of Can I Make a Recipe Go Viral? — Tushar's original French dip, rebuilt on crisp polenta instead of bread. Slice a chilled tube of prepared polenta into 12 rounds, oil and pepper them, and oven-crisp at 475°F. Warm a package of pre-cooked au jus beef, save the juices, and build a dipping jus with an au jus packet and a bone-broth packet. Cap six crisp rounds with provolone and beef, bake to melt, then top with the remaining rounds. Serve two dunkers, 2/3 cup citrus-seasoned green beans, and a ramekin of jus per plate. Keep the jus on the side so the polenta stays crisp. About 450 cal / 40g protein per plate — a sodium-forward build from the packaged beef, packets, cheese, and seasoning, so taste before adding any salt.
